value.title: Exact product and branchwise additivity of relaxed UV scalars
value.statement: For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel W, let t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z), define A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+C[-t_W](p) and D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+C[t_W](p), where C is the upper concave envelope on the input simplex, and set B_avg(W)=sup_p(A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2 and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. Then B_avg is exactly additive under arbitrary finite products of finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, including optimization over correlated product-channel input laws and envelope auxiliaries joint across factors. If a channel is receiver-skew, in the sense that an involutive input relabeling exchanges its receiver marginals up to output relabeling, then B_br(W)=B_avg(W), and the optimization may be restricted to invariant input laws. Finite products of receiver-skew channels preserve this property, so both scalar functionals are additive on every such finite product. For the half-skew BSSC P, the sharp one-letter posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving mixture supplied by result-code-induced-balance-entropy-copy-no-go give B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) bits for every integer n≥1.
scopeQualifications: The theorem concerns only the two separately relaxed scalar UV functionals. It does not establish tensorization of the full UV region, optimization over a common joint (U,V), the GK functional, the full Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem-9 system, broadcast-channel capacity, or capacity tensorization.

Exact additivity of B_avg holds for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBC products, while equality B_br=B_avg and the resulting additivity of B_br require receiver-skew involutive symmetry and its finite-product closure.

The dependency result is needed only for the global sharp BSSC posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving posterior mixture used in the half-skew BSSC specialization; the general product and receiver-skew arguments are established analytically within this result.
The README decimal approximation is inaccurate; the exact expression n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) is the established value and is unaffected.

The executable checker verifies selected numerical and algebraic identities, including the BSSC contact mixture and receiver-skew relations, but does not verify the global support inequality, concave-envelope optimization, or product theorem; those steps are discharged analytically.
The resulting separately relaxed BSSC scalar value supplies neither an achievability theorem nor a capacity formula or certified improvement of a governed capacity endpoint.

proofs: Conditional mutual-information chain rules and cancellation of cross-factor co-information terms bound each product-channel concave-envelope contribution by the corresponding one-factor contributions; mutual-information subadditivity then gives the product upper bound for B_avg, while product priors and product posterior decompositions give the reverse inequality.

Receiver-exchanging involutive relabeling exchanges A_W and D_W. Concavity and symmetrization yield an invariant input law attaining at least the averaged value in the branchwise minimum, while min{a,d}≤(a+d)/2 gives the reverse bound.

Coordinatewise receiver-skew involutions preserve the symmetry on finite products, and combining this closure with product additivity of B_avg proves finite-product additivity of both scalar functionals on the receiver-skew class.

For the half-skew BSSC, the dependency's global sharp posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving posterior mixture evaluate the one-letter envelopes at the invariant fair input law, yielding the exact value 2h_2(1/4)-5/4 per factor.
methods: Conditional mutual-information chain rules and co-information cancellation
computations: The submitted standard-library script evaluates the half-skew BSSC identities at high precision and checks the contact posterior mixture and receiver-skew channel relations. These checks are corroborative and do not replace the analytic product, envelope, or global-support arguments.
tools: The submitted Python standard-library verifier checks selected algebraic and numerical specialization identities.

value.title: Tensorization of relaxed UV sum-rate scalars
value.objective: Characterize product behavior, symmetry reductions, and BSSC implications of the separately relaxed UV sum-rate scalar functionals, and determine which richer converse structures remain capable of multiletter improvement.
value.currentStateSummary: The averaged separately relaxed UV scalar B_avg is exactly additive for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBC products, even with correlated product-channel input laws and joint envelope auxiliaries. For receiver-skew channels with an involutive receiver-exchanging input symmetry, B_br equals B_avg, invariant input laws suffice, and finite products preserve the symmetry; consequently both scalars are additive on every finite product of such channels. Using the established global sharp BSSC posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving mixture, the half-skew BSSC satisfies B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) for every n≥1. The exact expression governs despite an inaccurate README decimal approximation. This exhausts blocking as a strengthening mechanism for these two separately relaxed scalar rows, but it does not address a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the full UV region, the GK functional, richer Theorem-9 systems, or capacity itself.
value.localResidualSummary: Investigate converse structures absent from the additive separately relaxed scalars, including coupling of UV branches through a common joint law, exact BSSC posterior consistency, nonsymmetric branchwise behavior, and richer GK or full-Theorem-9 auxiliary constraints. Any extension must be proved independently and connected to a certified capacity bound; the present scalar theorem itself moves no capacity endpoint.

value.title: Canonical problem
value.currentStateSummary: Two complementary converse directions remain established. The code-induced structural direction shows that deterministic finite-block private-message codes obey approximate dependence balance, a fixed encoder-coordinate map, and four compatible rate rows, while an explicit nonbinary entropic witness obstructs the specified coarse entropy and finite copy-lemma refinement route; blocklength-dependent auxiliaries and exact BSSC posterior consistency remain unresolved. In the relaxed UV-scalar direction, B_avg is exactly additive for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBC products, receiver-skew symmetry gives B_br=B_avg, and finite products preserve that symmetry. With the global sharp BSSC posterior support, both separately relaxed scalars on P^{×n} equal n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4); the exact expression is unaffected by an inaccurate README decimal approximation. This scalar theorem concerns neither the full UV region nor common joint-(U,V), GK, full-Theorem-9, or capacity optimization, and it changes no capacity endpoint. The canonical capacity problem therefore remains unresolved.
value.localResidualSummary: Develop a fixed-cardinality reduction or exact binary-BSSC posterior and multiletter constraints for laws induced by genuine codes, excluding the nonbinary entropy witness where appropriate. Because the separately relaxed UV scalars tensorize at a non-frontier value, a stronger multiletter converse must retain structure absent from those scalars—such as coupling between UV branches, exact channel-consistent posteriors, or richer nested auxiliary and full-region constraints—and must ultimately yield a certified capacity improvement or resolution.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted claim establishes the same independently reusable tensorization, receiver-skew reduction, and half-skew BSSC specialization already represented by result-uv-product-branchwise-additivity. Its analytic proof and current evidence are therefore consolidated into that stable result rather than creating a duplicate result. The result remains under the objective-specific relaxed-UV-scalar tensorization program, with the sharp BSSC support result retained as its sole dependency. The affected leaf program and root ancestor are updated to synthesize the accepted theorem, its exact-value qualification, its strict scalar scope, and the remaining richer-converse directions.
